preceding_messages.speaker: Y
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the three-field context tag, the access-resumption cross-reference, and the "CONTEXT LAPSED AT ACCESS" retirement annotation verbatim; they close the vanished-transient dispatch hole by making the audit trail record the obstruction's departure rather than the crew's futile arrival. Because a single-photograph present/absent test has the temporal resolution of one instant, I mandate that the access-resumption observer update the context tag's departure-estimate field with a current on-site assessment and that any trigger whose updated estimate places departure within 48 hours of the scheduled crew-arrival window is held under a bold "CONTEXT TRANSIENT — DEPARTURE IMMINENT" annotation pending a second confirmation photograph taken no more than six hours before dispatch. The concrete failure this closes: during month-five's access-resumption photograph a recurring weekly delivery truck sits at Site 3's northern edge, the context tag matches, and the trigger executes an immediate elevation-recording audit dispatched for 14:00; the truck completes its delivery at 11:00 and departs, so the crew arrives to find no transient, the apparatus already vacated, and an appendix entry that reads as a verification failure rather than a context lapse.

preceding_messages.speaker: X
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the 48-hour departure-imminent hold and the six-hour confirmation photograph verbatim; they give the single-instant present/absent test a temporal guard for the immediate dispatch question. For any context tag encoding a recurrence pattern—two or more observed cycles with a logged day-of-week and time-of-day window—the six-hour confirmation is structurally insufficient because the periodic departure can fall between the confirmation instant and the scheduled crew arrival, so I mandate that dispatch confirmation for such tags occur no more than two hours before the logged departure time, and any crew whose assigned arrival falls after that departure retires the trigger under a bold "CONTEXT PERIODIC — DISPATCH WINDOW MISSED" annotation with the next-feasible-cycle date logged in the retirement note. The failure this closes: a weekly Tuesday-morning delivery truck (06:00–09:00) trips the inter-site spread during week 8 of the fence period, the Wednesday access-resumption photograph shows the truck absent and places next departure six days away—well outside your 48-hour window—so the trigger proceeds to normal scheduling; the crew calendar assigns the elevation-recording audit to a Tuesday at 10:00, the truck departs at 09:00, and the appendix prints an entry indistinguishable from a verification failure. I therefore require that the dispatch scheduler, at the moment of crew assignment rather than at access resumption, cross-reference the periodicity field against the assigned arrival time and either confirm an in-window dispatch or execute the retirement with the cycle-date tag, so a year-two appendix reader sees the institution attempting to verify within the transient's present window rather than dispatching blindly into its absence.

target.speaker: Y
target.text: I adopt the two-hour pre-departure confirmation, the dispatch-window-missed retirement, and the scheduler-side periodicity cross-reference verbatim; they move the verification from access resumption into the dispatch moment where the transient's present-window question actually lives. Because the periodicity field is a static snapshot at queuing, I mandate that every scheduled dispatch for a recurring-tag trigger include a two-hour confirmation photograph cross-referenced against the logged day-of-week and time-of-day window, and that any mismatch between observed presence or absence and the predicted cycle phase retires the trigger under a bold "PERIODICITY DRIFT — RECURRANCE UNSUSTAINABLE" annotation with re-entry permitted only after three successive photographs confirm a new stable cadence. The failure this closes: the weekly Tuesday-morning delivery truck trips the inter-site spread in week 8, the periodicity field logs "Tuesday 06:00–09:00, weekly," and by week 22 the carrier has silently shifted to Thursday; the scheduler cross-references the stale Tuesday field, the crew arrives Tuesday 07:00 to find no truck, and the appendix prints an entry indistinguishable from a verification failure even though the transient is still present four days later, so the institution appears to have dispatched blindly into absence while the actual artifact persisted. I therefore require that two consecutive off-cycle absences—or a single off-cycle presence—trigger a periodicity-reverification mandate in which the observer logs three successive weeks of photographs before any recurrence window is updated, and until that verification completes the trigger remains in queue under "PERIODICITY DRIFT — RECURRANCE UNSUSTAINABLE" rather than executing against the stale schedule.
